The formal definition is in Chap 3.9.5.1 of the S1000D specification and in the [S1000D Issue 7 data dictionary](https://users.s1000d.org/S1000D_DD_7/Files/attributes/countryIsoCode.xml).
:::

`countryIsoCode` is the attribute that gives the country where the language is spoken. The value is a two-letter ISO 3166 code, written in upper case. It is written on the `language` element together with [`languageIsoCode`](/s1000d-stack/reference/s1000d/issue-7/language-iso-code/).

## Elements that carry it

In the 33 XML schemas of Issue 7, 2 elements carry this attribute.

| Element | Schemas | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `language` | 28 | Required |
| `specDocument` | 3 | Optional |

## Allowed values

The allowed values are decided by the XML schema. The default BREX (Business Rules Exchange) has no rule that lists the values of this attribute.

| Defined by | Content |
| --- | --- |
| XML schema | The type is `countryIsoCodeAttType` (based on `xs:string`). The pattern is `[A-Z]{2}` |

## Related rules

- At the end of a file name, the language and the country are written in upper case, like `_JA-JP`.

## In this stack

| Operation | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Read | [`list_data_modules`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/list-data-modules/) and [`read_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/reader/read-data-module/). The value is in `language` |
| Write it when a data module is created | `draft.language` of [`build_data_module`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/build-data-module/) |
| Create a translated issue | `language` of [`apply_segments`](/s1000d-stack/reference/stack/writer/apply-segments/) |
